findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell command
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, `exec()` interprets it rather than passing it solely to Git. An input such as `main; arbitrary-command` therefore executes another command with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation treated the value as an inert argument and avoided this vulnerability.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the spawned Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than necessarily the `git` process. On Windows, or when a valid branch name contains shell operators such as `|` or `&`, Git runs as a descendant; calling `kill()` on the returned `ChildProcess` can terminate only the shell while Git continues, and the shell may report exit before Git finishes. The previous `execFile()` return value directly represented Git.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell command
findings.body:
`exec` evaluates `branch` as shell syntax, allowing arbitrary command execution under the application’s privileges. For example, the valid Git branch name `x;touch${IFS}/tmp/proof` executes `touch /tmp/proof`; the previous `execFile` implementation passed it as an inert argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` without escaping. If an attacker can influence the branch value, input such as `main; arbitrary-command` executes with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile()` implementation passed the branch as a separate argument and was not vulnerable to shell metacharacters.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names in argv to prevent uncontrolled subprocess execution
findings.body:
`exec` evaluates `branch` through a shell. Even ref-valid input such as `topic;sleep${IFS}60` runs `sleep 60` after `git show`; repeated calls can retain unbounded processes and pipes or execute a fork bomb, exhausting the host. The previous `execFile` passed this text only as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
